summary: Tenant prefetch spin-up causing intermittent 5xx sawtooth and runtime hotpath lock contention
description: Issue summary: VisionaryChat reported a multi-minute window of elevated 502/503 responses for chat endpoints across us-west and us-east. The pattern is a sawtooth (rapid rise/fall) of 5xx rate coincident with tenant-initiated prefetch spin-ups. Impact: Several customer agents experienced degraded availability during high concurrency warm-ups; customer reported increased user-visible errors and retries. Environment: prod (us-west primary, traffic mirrored to us-east). Hypothesis: prefetcher + runtime hotpath lock ordering creates transient deadlock/long-hold on runtime request queue leading to proxy upstream 502/503s and queued conn backpressure on api-gateway.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant, send a steady low-rate of chat requests for 5 minutes. 2) Trigger a high-concurrency burst (20x baseline) that causes the tenant prefetcher to warm multiple model shards. 3) Observe api-gateway 5xx rate and runtime thread stacks for kvcache/prefetch lock holds. 4) Repeat with and without prefetch enabled to compare.
logs: Relevant logs: apigw/2026-03-10T18:02:14Z 502 upstream reset; runtime/worker-12 2026-03-10T18:02:14Z blocking on prefetch::ShardLock for 8.3s; stackdump: serving::batch_queue -> prefetch::lock -> kv_store::writeback -> scheduler::try_alloc. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/987-prefetch/tenant-5xx-sawtooth and trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/0af4-prefetch-spinup. Extract: "runtime: blocking on ShardLock; concurrent_prefetch=12; accept_queue=120/128"
timeline: 2026-03-10 17:58 UTC - Customer reported elevated errors. 2026-03-10 18:00 UTC - Support triaged and escalated to SRE. 18:05 UTC - SRE observed sawtooth 5xx aligned with tenant prefetch spikes. 18:15 UTC - Temporary mitigation: routed 30% traffic away from tenant, increased runtime pool by 2 nodes, disabled prefetch for tenant. 18:40 UTC - 5xx rates dropped to baseline. 2026-03-11 - Engineering reproduced locally, identified lock-order inversion in prefetch hotpath. 2026-03-12 - Hotfix PR opened and staged to canary; further rollout planned.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: GPU overload during shard warmup causing watchdog resets — not supported by NVML metrics (no driver resets).
Observed long-held mutexes in runtime worker stacks centered on prefetch::ShardLock and scheduler allocation path.
Correlation: api-gateway accept_queue fills during prefetch spikes; 502s originate when upstream runtime cannot accept new streams for >1s.
Reproduction: synthetic burst with prefetch enabled reproduces 5xx sawtooth; toggling prefetch disables the pattern.
Root cause draft: lock-order inversion between kvcache writeback path and scheduler allocation triggers long critical-section holds when concurrent prefetchers contend for shard metadata.
Customer impact: retries observable in VisionaryChat logs; increase in user-perceived failures by ~4% during window.
Related incidents: SUP-412345 (model-stage-swap 5xx spike) shows similar accept_queue dynamics but different root cause.
Mitigations tried: route-weight shift, temporary prefetch disable, runtime scale-up — all reduced surface but required code fix for long term.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer first reported at 17:58 UTC — they saw a ~6 minute window of errors, attached sample request IDs.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Confirmed sawtooth pattern on grafana; increased runtime pool and disabled prefetch for tenant as stopgap.
Priya Nair (Eng) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally; attaching perftrace and locking profiles. Suspect lock-order inversion in prefetcher + kv writeback.
Diego Alvarez 2026-03-11: After temporary disables, error-rate normalized. Planning hotfix to change lock ordering + add bounded prefetch concurrency per-tenant.
VisionaryChat (customer) 2026-03-11: Appreciated rapid mitigation; asked for root cause and ETA for permanent fix.
resolution_notes: Short-term: disabled tenant prefetch and increased runtime pool which restored availability. Temporary route reweight reduced user impact. Long-term: merged hotfix that enforces consistent lock ordering and adds bounded prefetch concurrency per-tenant (PR 1824). Deployed to canary 2026-03-12 and to 50% of prod 2026-03-12; full rollout targeted 2026-03-13 after monitoring window. Follow-ups: add prefetch chaos test to CI, instrument per-shard lock hold histograms, update runbook with mitigation steps and customer communication template.
